title: Explicit legacy CIRCLE/ARC inverse extrusion for bounded AC1024 DWG output
supportClaimEffect: bounded explicit helper contract only; no broad DWG or 3D claim

authority.oda: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1 sections 20.4.18 and 20.4.20 specify CIRCLE/ARC center, radius, thickness and extrusion and ARC start/end angles.

change: Document that the existing explicit DRW_DxfLegacyExtrusion::toNativeOcs helper may be used before the bounded AC1024 DWG writer route. This changes no runtime implementation, class layout, vtable, default reader/writer behavior, or automatic frame inference. The caller must still guarantee exactly one legacy applyExtrusion call, unchanged relevant coordinates/normal/flag, and exact built-in entity types. It does not represent a general WCS ARC-angle conversion; other DWG revisions remain unqualified.

physicalSource.method: tools/author_dwg_legacy_extrusion.py authored a scratch R2010 DXF with tilted (0,1,0) and axial-negative (0,0,-1) CIRCLE/ARC entities and nonzero thickness; ODA File Converter 27.1.0 wrote AC1024 DWG. tools/replay_dwg_legacy_extrusion.cpp reads that physical source with applyExt=true, explicitly converts the selected entities and writes a new AC1024 DWG using the bounded material/plotstyle opt-in providers. This is selected geometry, not a whole-document copy. ODA converted both DWGs to DXF with no error files.
physicalSource.independent: tests/dwg_legacy_extrusion_oda_ezdxf.py compared all four ODA-exported entities using ezdxf 1.4.5: OCS centers, normals, radii and thicknesses, WCS centers, ARC angles and WCS endpoints match. Rebuilt tracked replay tool reproduced the identical converted DWG hash.

generatedSource.method: The focused C++ test generates AC1024 DWGs from scratch, reads raw and applyExt views, converts explicitly, writes, and checks both raw and applied readback. It also refuses an invalid second-entity normal without changing an existing destination, then corrects and retries with the same dwgRW facade.
generatedSource.normals: six each of CIRCLE and ARC: identity, negative Z, tilted, nonunit and both sides of the arbitrary-axis cutoff. ODA converted both generated DWGs with no error files; ezdxf independently matched all 12 OCS fields, WCS centers and ARC endpoints.

reproduction: Convert source and converted DWGs to separate DXFs with ODA, then run tests/dwg_legacy_extrusion_oda_ezdxf.py <source.dxf> <converted.dxf> 4. Bind all observations to exact per-run SHA-256 hashes; newly generated source IDs/hashes may differ.

For generated controls, run build-gcc/tests/libdxfrw_dxf_legacy_extrusion_tests --keep, convert its ac1024-original.dwg and ac1024-converted.dwg with ODA, then compare the resulting DXFs using the same script with count 12.
limits: Only selected CIRCLE/ARC geometry under the stated AC1024 writer providers is checked; source metadata, other object graphs and whole-file fidelity are not qualified.

The physical source has two normals and four entities; generated peer checks broaden arithmetic coverage but do not establish native semantic behavior for every producer, arbitrary edit or general 3D geometry.
